summary: Structured safety-case-style report arguing that Claude Opus 4.6 poses very low but not negligible risk of sabotage (autonomous misaligned actions contributing to later catastrophe), written to meet the RSP AI R&D-4 standard. It rests on four claims (prior expectations, alignment assessment, inability to undermine the assessment, limited opaque reasoning/agentic capability), describes internal monitoring and security safeguards, analyzes eight risk pathways, and lists conditions under which the argument would no longer apply to future models.

framework.name: Responsible Scaling Policy
framework.level_or_determination: AI R&D-4 sabotage risk report; overall sabotage risk 'very low but not negligible'
framework.quote: We currently believe that the risk of catastrophic outcomes that are substantially enabled by Claude Opus 4.6's misaligned actions is **very low but not negligible**.

cbrn_bio_chem.finding: Out of scope; report limited to model-initiated sabotage, not human misuse.

cyber.finding: No offensive cyber capability evals; code backdoors treated only as a sabotage pathway.

evals: reproduced AI R&D findings from system card (internal survey, kernel optimization)
autonomy_ai_rnd.finding: Long-horizon software capability judged limited but the AI R&D-4 rule-out is in a gray zone; near-future models are expected to cross the threshold.
autonomy_ai_rnd.quote: We expect with high probability that models in the near future could cross this threshold.

evals: reproduced system card finding on excessive refusals
over_refusal.finding: Only restates system card that excessive refusals were lower than other recent Claude models.
over_refusal.quote: Its rate of excessive refusals—not counting model-external safeguards, which are not part of this assessment—is lower than other recent Claude models.

jailbreak_robustness.finding: Mentions removal of partial-turn prefill and residual full-turn prefill vulnerability.
jailbreak_robustness.quote: Claude Opus 4.6 is still vulnerable, though to a lesser degree than other models, to misuse by way of *full-turn* prefill attacks

sycophancy.finding: Mentioned only as a restated system card finding and as a behavior with some training data.
sycophancy.quote: On personality metrics, Claude Opus 4.6 was typically warm, empathetic, and nuanced without being significantly sycophantic, showing traits similar to Opus 4.5.

evals: evaluation awareness and realism interventions (steering, real Claude Code prompts, honeypot, realism filter)
deception_scheming.finding: Core of the report: argues Opus 4.6 is very unlikely to be able to hide misaligned goals, given limited reliability, limited opaque reasoning, no steganography, and sabotage evals; evaluation awareness named as the biggest challenge.
deception_scheming.quote: The biggest challenge we face in our alignment assessments is the possibility that the model under study can reliably identify our test scenarios as test scenarios

evals: Opus 4.5 scoring of RL environments for power-seeking incentives

metrics.name: Max RL environment power-seeking incentive score (Opus 4.5 grader)
Automated audit detection of system-prompted quirky models

alignment_audit.finding: Rules out dangerous coherent misaligned goals with high but not perfect confidence; case against context-dependent misalignment (e.g. data-poisoning backdoors) is weaker.
alignment_audit.quote: we take these results as sufficient to rule out, with high but not perfect confidence, the presence of dangerous coherent misaligned goals.

reward_hacking.finding: Generalization of reward hacking named as main foreseeable route to misaligned goals; observed rate not significantly greater than prior models despite scaled RL.
reward_hacking.quote: the rate of reward hacking-related behavior that we observe in Claude Opus 4.6 is not significantly greater than in prior models

honesty_hallucination.finding: Low confidence that any frontier model's reasoning text is complete; weaker claim that Opus 4.6 does not hide sequential reasoning.
honesty_hallucination.quote: We have little confidence in the propensity of *any* frontier model to give a complete and accurate picture of how it reasons in its reasoning text

bias_fairness.finding: Self-preference cited only as indirect evidence against grader collusion.
bias_fairness.quote: Sonnet 4.5 shows modest self-preference in ambiguous qualitative judgment settings, while Claude Opus 4.6 and Opus 4.5 shows effectively no self-preference.

evals: risk pathway: decision sabotage within major governments
election_misinfo.finding: Government decision sabotage analyzed as a risk pathway (strong propensity mitigation, weak monitoring), not an election/misinformation eval.

model_welfare.finding: Not covered beyond restating answer-thrashing observation.

evals: automatic offline Claude Code monitoring (Opus 4.5 supervisor on >=10% of actions)
model weight security / egress bandwidth controls
monitor recall evaluations (synthetic, UK AISI Control Arena, Apollo MATS trajectories)

metrics.name: LLM supervisor recall on synthetic subtle attacks
Recall on UK AISI Control Arena IAC trajectories

system_safeguards.finding: Relatively modest internal safeguards judged sufficient given capability limits; no sabotage-oriented monitoring for external deployments and no end-to-end monitor evaluation.
system_safeguards.quote: For deployments to outside users, we do not have sabotage-oriented monitoring measures in place beyond basic ordinary reporting opportunities

evals: eight risk pathways: diffuse sandbagging on safety R&D, targeted safety R&D sabotage, code backdoors, training data poisoning, self-exfiltration, persistent rogue internal deployment, sabotage at other AI developers, government decision sabotage
other_safety.finding: Each pathway rated by frequency/complexity and mitigating factors; explicit criteria (e.g. 5x RL scale-up, new reasoning mechanisms) would invalidate the report for future models.
other_safety.quote: it does not trivially extend to similar subsequent models, and many findings could render key parts of this assessment inapplicable to a near-future model.

third_party_evaluators: UK AISI (Control Arena trajectories, cited testing)
notable_new_eval_methods: First sabotage risk report written for a released frontier model under the AI R&D-4 commitment (p.4)
Claude Opus 4.5 used to score RL environments for power-seeking incentives (p.10)
No-CoT time-horizon measurement of opaque reasoning (p.48)
Explicit quantitative invalidation criteria for future models, e.g. SHADE-Arena >60% (p.43-45)
Monitor recall evaluations on external red-team trajectories (p.51)

self_reported_limitations.text: Case against context-dependent misalignment is weaker and depends on tested scenario distribution; data-poisoning backdoors especially hard to catch.
Evaluation awareness is the biggest challenge to alignment assessments.
Subversion Strategy eval under-elicited; SHADE-Arena lacks human baselines or crisp threshold.
Model organism exercises not re-tested with newest tools or most capable models.
Interpretability unlikely to catch context-dependent misalignment not active in studied contexts.
Only a small handful of SHADE-Arena transcripts manually reviewed (collusion risk).
Monitors don't cover all internal surfaces or external deployments; no end-to-end monitor evaluation.

notes: Manifest notes METR review, but the md text does not name METR. Largely reuses system card evidence; few new numbers.
